title: React Native Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this React Native course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: Which component displays words?
exercises.explanation: A View groups native page parts. Text displays words. These components are the building blocks of a React Native screen.

exercises.question: How is the background property named?
exercises.explanation: StyleSheet.create groups styles under names. Native style properties use JavaScript names such as backgroundColor.

exercises.question: Which prop handles a native button press?
exercises.explanation: React state remembers a value between renders. A native Button calls onPress when activated.

exercises.question: What value does onChangeText provide?
exercises.explanation: TextInput lets someone type text. onChangeText supplies the new text, so state can keep the field and screen together.

exercises.question: What is React Native's default flex direction?
exercises.explanation: React Native uses Flexbox for layout. Its default direction is a column, so set row when items should sit beside each other.

exercises.question: Which component is a better choice for a very large list?
exercises.explanation: ScrollView makes its children scrollable. It is useful for a limited amount of content that can be rendered together.

exercises.question: What does keyExtractor return?
options: A stable id for each row
exercises.explanation: FlatList receives data and a function for each row. It can avoid keeping every distant row rendered at once.

exercises.question: Where does this picture come from?
exercises.explanation: Image displays a native picture. A local file can be bundled with require so the app can include it at build time.

exercises.question: What does the pressed value tell the style callback?
options: Whether the control is being pressed
Whether the app has a user account
exercises.explanation: Pressable can wrap a custom control. Its style callback receives pressed, so the control can show a clear response.

exercises.question: Why use safe-area insets?
options: To save every app file online
To avoid placing content under system cutouts and bars
exercises.explanation: Some screens have cutouts or system bars. Safe-area components add space so important content does not sit under those areas.

exercises.question: What does ListEmptyComponent handle?
exercises.explanation: A useful list explains when it has no items. FlatList can render a dedicated empty component.

exercises.question: What does this demo use to choose a view?
options: A complete native route history automatically
exercises.explanation: State can choose between two simple views while learning. A real navigation library adds history and platform navigation behaviour for larger apps.
